brief: UBS's Curtis frames Jensen Huang's exit as a big deal: debate holds it could take ~18 months before effects hit Nvidia products, with open questions on remaining Nvidia downside and possible upside for AVGO. Curtis stays bearish on semis (and software, too high again), arguing sell-siders should cut 2028 numbers 20% to close the gap between chip estimates and power-infrastructure capacity, since he doubts post-election supply concerns are already discounted; a reset needs management to admit double/triple ordering. Separately, Tim's prior Nvidia note warns the departure could pause roughly $50B/quarter of ecosystem financing and Nvidia's supply-chain lead just as credit tightens, and that tighter export limits on NVDA/AMD into China, Singapore and Malaysia could hit about 10% of Nvidia revenue (Singapore alone was near 20% before Nvidia stopped disclosing it). On Cerebras, shares jumped high-teens after results: hardware sales offset industry-wide data-center power delays, and new Microsoft and OCI deals plus an early Amazon ramp diversify the base, but OpenAI still drives EPS and cut its RPO, which UBS blames on power delays letting OpenAI claim contract credits. UBS trimmed its CBRS estimates and price target to $155, kept Buy, calling the OpenAI concern overdone.
